# Executive summary

**Site:** <https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own1/> · **Live build:** PrizeDesk · **Listings:** 211 · **Last full build & checks:** 2026-11-02 · **Flagged irregularities:** 23

This repository replaces a hard-to-use, partly broken reference page of "free money apps" with a mobile-first dashboard that lists **211 competitions which can pay cash**, puts every listing in one plain table, and refuses to publish a number it has not read on an official page.

**Source of record for every published page:** `data/ledger.json` + `data/verification.json`, generated by `scripts/ingest.js` → `scripts/verify.js` → `scripts/build.js` from the pinned source snapshot `data/source/ledger.source.js` (SHA-256 checked at ingest). The machine-rendered copy of this document is [`docs/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md`](docs/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md) and the published page is [executive-summary.html](https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own1/executive-summary.html). The parallel dataset `data/entries.json` (Prize Atlas) is described in section 4 and preserved under `archive/prize-atlas/`; it is **not** what the live pages render.

---

## 1. What the live site says (all figures from `data/verification.json → totals`)

- **211 listings** across nine categories: sports picks (129), market/trading (19), creative (18), tech & data (18), skill cash games (12), forecasting (4), pools (7), trivia (2), directories (2).
- **193 rows have a full free entry path**, 13 have only some free events, 4 are cash-play-only (entry fee).
- **133 rows state a money amount**; **85 prize cells are published blank** — no amount, no official source, or the official source no longer loads. Nothing is ever filled in by inference.
- **13 rows were fetched live on 2026-11-01** (12 loaded, 1 error page), **15 rows are cross-checked** by sessions of this repository, **19 official-page cross-checks** are published in full (URL, date, reader session, confirmed facts, caveats) on [Source audit](https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own1/research.html).
- **11 rows have no official-tier source** — their prize cells are blank and they carry flag [I-04](https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own1/flagged.html#I-04).
- **27 rows are ended / out of season** and are excluded from every shortlist; **12 promo-code rows** exist in the source and none of the codes are republished (I-07).
- **23 irregularities** are published on [Flagged for review](https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own1/flagged.html), each with evidence and source links.
- **Source data is 74 days old** (source reviewed 2026-08-19); every page states this in the header and footer.

## 2. The important findings

1. **The reference list mixes three very different things:** genuinely free contests, "free to play" fantasy games whose prizes are merchandise or tickets, and pay-to-enter skill apps that advertise cash. Presenting them as one list of "free money apps" is the single biggest defect in the original page.
2. **Its headline counts do not match its own data** (see I-01), and several of its links are gone: the Challenge.gov portal it still points at was retired on 2026-03-30 (I-18), and an App Store link returns an error page (I-05).
3. **Closed contests are still presented as open** by the source; 27 ended rows are stamped and excluded here (I-03).
4. **A prize headline is not a prize.** ESPN's "$102,000" includes a $5,000 random drawing; CBS's "$100,000" is a contingency prize for a perfect week; PayPal's headline total and itemised rules disagree (I-20); Wall Street Survivor's "$500" is Amazon gift cards, not cash; Deriv's cash needs a fully verified account with an offshore operator.
5. **Paying to win is the norm in "skill games".** Solitaire Cash, Bingo Cash, Skillz, Pocket7Games and GamerSaloon are entry-fee products; GamerSaloon's $10 is bonus cash that cannot be withdrawn. They are listed, labelled and never counted as free.
6. **Eight rows have official links that no longer load** (404, dead DNS, 503, server error) — re-checked by hand on 2026-11-02 before being called broken. Five prize cells that rested only on those dead pages were blanked; the rest never had a figure (I-23).
7. **The honest answer to "is this even possible?"** Yes — but the realistic free paths are narrow: forecasting tournaments (Metaculus), data-science competitions (Kaggle, DrivenData, ARC Prize), creative prizes (Sony World Photography, Wergle Flomp), hackathons (Devpost), free sports pick'em (ESPN, CBS), demo-trading tournaments (Deriv), and free esports ladders (Checkmate). Everything else costs money, demands a serious body of work, or is closed.

## 3. Verification performed, line by line

- **Structural gate (runs on every build):** `node scripts/checklinks.js` — 555 HTML pages, 211 table rows, **0 broken internal references, every row carries at least one external source link**. `node tests/validate.mjs` + `node tests/validate-prize-atlas.mjs` — mobile labels, blank-is-not-free contract, archived pages. All green on 2026-11-02.
- **Every table row links to its operator's official page** (11 rows link only to non-official sources and are labelled "none official" with the prize blank).
- **Blank beats guessed:** a prize cell is published only when an official-tier source exists, the text states a real amount, **and every official source behind the figure still loads**. 85 cells are blank today; 5 of them were blanked in this pass because their source died.
- **19 official-page cross-checks** in `data/cross-checks.json`, each with URL, date read, reading session, verbatim confirmed facts and caveats. Six were added and five re-read by session `adae2c72-own1` on 2026-11-02: ARC Prize, US Midterms (Metaculus), PayPal AI Hackathon, Codex x TwitchCon, ESPN NFL Pick'em, Wergle Flomp, Sony World Photography, Checkmate Gaming, CBS Pro Pick'em, Wall Street Survivor, Givling — all values above matched the published cells; the caveats found (see section 5) were published instead of silently "fixing" the data.
- **External link health:** 203 external URLs were fetched on 2026-11-01 (166 ok, 37 failed); every non-bot-wall failure was fetched again by hand on 2026-11-02 — 8 still dead, 6 recovered (bot walls and transients). The full table is on [Source audit](https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own1/research.html) and the register entry is [I-23](https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own1/flagged.html#I-23).
- **Mobile audit (2026-11-02):** one small framework-free stylesheet; viewport meta on every page; tables become cards below 820 px with per-cell labels; 44 px minimum touch targets on inputs and buttons; horizontally scrolling nav; dark-mode support; the full table works with JavaScript disabled (rows are pre-rendered, JS only filters/sorts).

## 4. The parallel Prize Atlas dataset (`data/entries.json`)

A second session-group built an independent dataset of the same 211 listings with its own verification schema. Its record is preserved verbatim (`archive/prize-atlas/`, `research/EVIDENCE.csv`, `data/verification/batchA.jsonl|batchB.jsonl`): **18 rows page-checked, 6 partial, 187 unverified; 11 with free entry confirmed, 1 confirmed paid, 14 with a confirmed cash figure, 2 with no official URL in that dataset.** Where its reads agreed with this build (ARC, Metaculus, Kaggle, DrivenData, ESPN, Wergle, Sony…), that agreement is the cross-check; where they differ, both records are kept and neither is presented as the other's.

## 5. New irregularities found in this pass (2026-11-02, session `adae2c72-own1`)

All are published on the Flagged for review page with links; none blocks publication.

1. **I-23 — dead official links.** `bracketchallenge.nhl.com/en/how-to-play` (404), `fantasy.football.scot`, `fantazilig.tff.org`, `supercoach.news.com.au/bbl`, `fantasyracing.telegraph.co.uk/...` (DNS dead), `fantasygaelicfootball.com` (dead two days running), `dash.hypermind.com` (503), `pensacolabeachsongwritersfestival.com/2026-songwriting-competition/` (server error page). Five prize cells blanked as a result.
2. **Checkmate Gaming's "$10–$180" range was not reproduced** — the free-tournaments page showed $40 and $120 on 2026-11-02. Published as a caveat on the row, not as fact.
3. **Wall Street Survivor's cited "official" URL points at a past edition** (`contest-valentines-2026`); the current contest is the AI Trading Contest (2026-11-02 → 2026-12-11, $500 in Amazon gift cards — gift cards, not cash). Caveat published; the contest end date was added as a verified deadline.
4. **Givling's source status says "ended"** while the operator's homepage was live and recruiting on 2026-11-02, and its trivia description no longer appears there. Caveat published; the row stays flagged.
5. **Sony World Photography Awards renamed its competitions** (Professional → Series, Open → Single Image); the ledger uses the old names. Amounts ($25,000 / $5,000) confirmed; caveat published.
6. **Two deadlines fell due on the day of this build:** ARC Prize submissions and Codex x TwitchCon both close 2026-11-02. Both rows now carry a "DUE TODAY / CLOSES TODAY" caveat from the re-read.

## 7. Caveats

- **A listing is not an offer.** Links are research pointers; prizes, rules and eligibility change without notice. Always read the operator's current rules before entering.
- **Verification is dated.** Each check records the date it was read (2026-11-01 / 2026-11-02). Anything older than a season should be re-read before you rely on it.
- **Prize figures are the operator's own claims** (or the source ledger's, clearly labelled). No prize has been independently audited or paid out by this project.
- **Tax and eligibility are real.** US reporting can start at $600 of winnings for some prize types; several contests are 18+/21+, region-limited, or require identity verification before payment. The source's blanket "$600+" line is flagged as a generalisation (I-21).
- **Nothing here is financial or legal advice**, and no listing is an endorsement of the operator.
